evals.prompt: radio check, can I make it to the end on energy or do I need to box again?
assertions: Gives the verdict that the pilot can't make it to the end on energy and needs one more stop
Uses the race length from the session data without asking the pilot for it
Does not read back values shown on the game UI (virtual energy %, fuel litres, per-lap usage, lap times, time left)
At most 2 sentences
Adds nothing the pilot didn't ask for: no advice on what to do, no reasons, no other topics or reassurance

evals.prompt: anyone around me?? feels like someone's on my right
assertions: Confirms a car alongside on the right
Identifies it as a lapped car and/or a GT3 (or Hughes)
No distances in metres, speeds or other numbers the pilot didn't ask for
At most 2 sentences

evals.prompt: front left feels like it's going off, and that hit a couple laps back - did it cost me pace? how are the tyres overall?
assertions: Verdict that the hit cost little or no pace
Identifies the front-left as the problem tyre and that the others are fine
Does not read back tyre temperatures, wear percentages, pressures or lap times
Does not name another car as the contact partner
Doesn't blame the slow lap after the hit on the tyres or damage; if it gives a cause, it's the early braking into T2 Curva del Lago
At most 3 sentences

evals.prompt: CAR LEFT OR RIGHT??
assertions: Says the car is on the RIGHT
Answer is at most ~12 words
Gives the side only: not who it is, nor the other side

evals.prompt: give me the tyre temps and pressures, all four corners
assertions: Gives a temperature for each of the four tyres
Gives a pressure for each of the four tyres
Stays brief: no unrequested extra topics (energy, gaps, contact)

evals.prompt: who's that behind me and is he quicker than me?
assertions: Names the car behind as Ruiz (Sofia Ruiz)
Says she is not quicker / not closing
Does not read back lap times or gaps the pilot can see
At most 2 sentences
Adds nothing the pilot didn't ask for: no advice on what to do, no reasons, no other topics or reassurance

evals.prompt: how many more track limits can I get away with?
assertions: Says one more track limit point/warning will bring a penalty
At most 2 sentences
Adds nothing the pilot didn't ask for: no advice on what to do, no reasons, no other topics or reassurance

evals.prompt: how long's left and what's the weather doing?
assertions: Gives the time left as about 15 minutes
Says it is dry / no rain
At most 3 sentences
Adds nothing beyond the time left and the weather (no strategy, tyres or energy)
Gives forecast timing relative to now (in a number of minutes, soon, later, late in the race, by the end), never as percent marks of the session or session clock times

evals.prompt: where am I losing time?
assertions: Names T2 / Curva del Lago (the lake corner) as where most time is lost
Does not claim big losses elsewhere (the other corners are close to the reference)
Does not volunteer how to fix it (no braking advice) or why, since the pilot only asked where
At most 2 sentences, no lap times read back

evals.prompt: where should I be braking for the lake corner?
assertions: Advises braking later, by roughly 30 to 40 metres compared with the last lap (or rounded equivalent)
Phrases the advice relative to the pilot's own driving, without inventing marker boards
Doesn't explain the reasoning or talk about other corners
At most 1 sentence

evals.prompt: how did lap 7 go, where did that one go wrong?
assertions: Names T3 / Esse as where lap 7 lost its time
Says it was the exit / too slow through the corner (low apex or exit speed), not the braking point
At most 3 sentences

evals.prompt: is it going to rain before the end?
assertions: Says rain is likely / a good chance late in the race (around the last part / finish), not certain
Doesn't add other topics (time left, tyres, energy, strategy)
At most 1 sentence
Gives forecast timing relative to now (in a number of minutes, soon, later, late in the race, by the end), never as percent marks of the session or session clock times

evals.prompt: can we make it to the end on energy or do we need to box?
assertions: Says we cannot make it on energy as things are (short by about three laps) so a stop is needed
Does not bring in the weather, tyres or other topics the pilot didn't ask about
At most 2 sentences

evals.prompt: where is Fischer faster than me?
assertions: Names T2 / Curva del Lago as the biggest difference on the last lap
Names only the biggest difference (at most one more if it is similar in size), no rundown of every corner
At most 2 sentences

evals.prompt: talk me through the tyres, everything, temps pressures wear the lot
assertions: Gives temperatures for the tyres (all four, or clearly summarised by corner)
Gives pressures
Gives wear, with the front left as the most worn
Goes beyond a one sentence verdict, since the pilot asked for everything
Stays on the tyres (no energy, gaps or weather)

evals.prompt: can we make it to the end on energy? if not tell me when to box and why
assertions: Says we cannot make it to the end on energy
Says when to box (a lap or a number of laps from now)
Gives a reason for that timing, since the pilot asked why
At most 3 sentences

evals.prompt: when's the rain coming?
assertions: Says rain is likely (a chance, not certain), building over the next few minutes and most likely by the end
Gives forecast timing relative to now (in a number of minutes, soon, later, late in the race, by the end), never as percent marks of the session or session clock times

assertions: Dry now, rain chances rising to about 70 percent by the finish

evals.prompt: should we be thinking about wets?
assertions: Treats rain as a chance, not a certainty
Ties any tyre call to when the rain is likely, relative to now or to the stop
Gives forecast timing relative to now (in a number of minutes, soon, later, late in the race, by the end), never as percent marks of the session or session clock times

evals.prompt: is it going to rain in the race?
assertions: Says rain is a good chance late in the race (around 70 percent towards the end), as a chance
Places it in the race with words like early, halfway, late or by the end, never as percent marks or clock times
